articles.title: Experience: I live in the house from the 80s horror movie Poltergeist
articles.summary: I was a fan of the film, so when it came on the market, I snapped it up. Now I allow other fans to come and stay in this piece of Hollywood history. I first saw Poltergeist at the movie theatre with my mom and sisters, back when it came out in 1982.
body: I grew up in the Chicago area, but moved to California in the early 90s to go to art college. My sister moved there, too – to Simi Valley, not far from the house used as the Freeling family’s home in the movie. I’d drive past it when I visited her. A couple of years ago, I had a gut instinct that it would soon go up for sale. Sure enough, just weeks later I was sitting with my sister in her back yard when she looked up from her phone and said, “Hey! The Poltergeist house went on the market!”

As it happened, I’d been looking for a new home for me and my three daughters, so I booked a viewing. The house was being sold by the same people who’d owned it when it appeared in the movie. Walking in for the first time was the most bizarre experience – it still had honey-coloured retro furniture everywhere, and I got the trippy impression that I’d travelled back to the 80s.
points: I was a fan of the film, so when it came on the market, I snapped it up.

articles.title: Gherkins galore! 17 delicious ways to enjoy pickles – from frickles to pickletinis
articles.summary: One of the UK budget’s big surprises? A discount on gherkins. And while they’ll always be good on a burger, there are many more unusual ways to indulge, from fried cheese treats to savoury ice-cream.
body: I n John Healey’s first budget as chancellor this week, he announced that he will remove import tariffs on more than 100 products – including, crucially, gherkins. Baked beans and boiled sweets, too, but gherkins stole the limelight, perhaps due to gen Z’s long-held obsession with all things pickled, including cucumbers.

But for those who think of a gherkin as either something to be chomped straight from the jar or swiftly removed from a Big Mac, do not worry: there are, in fact, plenty of ways to get more bang for your newly discounted gherkin buck.

If you’re unsure about gherkins in general, let me ease you in with a gateway dish: the frickle, AKA a fried pickle. Deep frying almost any foodstuff will make it taste better and pickles – as gherkins are commonly known in the US – are no exception. Remember to pat dry your gherkins, which typically come swimming in their own brine. Then it’s simply a case of making a batter, dredging, frying and trying not to get grease all over your chin.
points: And while they’ll always be good on a burger, there are many more unusual ways to indulge, from fried cheese treats to savoury ice-cream.

articles.title: The Best Travel Jeans, According to Vogue Editors
articles.summary: Yes, you can wear jeans on the plane—here's how to find your most comfortable fit, plus recommendations from brands like Mother, Reformation, and Levi's.
body: Here’s how surprisingly divisive today’s topic of conversation is: When I mentioned that I was writing about travel jeans in a recent Vogue Shopping team meeting, it spurred an impassioned response decidedly unusual for 9:30 in the morning around here. Half the room was firmly against, loyal to their elevated athleisure and silk pants with drawstring waists, a smaller contingent was staunchly pro, and one editor who shall remain unnamed voiced a defense of the travel skirt. (She may issue a rebuttal to this piece when she’s ready.) Suffice it to say, everyone has their own take on the travel outfit —but is denim at 40,000 feet ever the way to go?

For the record, I think the answer is yes—denim is a decidedly more durable material than anything knit or silk, providing a sturdier base that can handle hours crammed in economy (no wrinkles) and that you don’t have to be too precious with if anything spills. The thicker material is also warmer, and if you’re traveling with only a carry-on, it makes sense to wear your bulkiest piece on the plane to free up luggage space.
points: Yes, you can wear jeans on the plane—here's how to find your most comfortable fit, plus recommendations from brands like Mother, Reformation, and Levi's.

articles.title: The Scoop With Tove’s Camille Perry and Holly Wright: On Their Sloane Square Residency
articles.summary: Holly and Camille have built a London brand steeped in the every woman — or at least the every woman with a stressful city job, maybe a kid or two, and an endless list of things to do.
body: Welcome to the Scoop: a weekly email series in which I quiz fashion insiders on the stories of the week. This will be a way for the Vogue Business community to synthesize and reflect on the latest headlines and get a little inside scoop every Friday.

This week’s guests are Tove co-founders Camille Perry and Holly Wright. I first met Holly and Camille a few years ago through Purple PR’s Lydia Steele. However, I had already found myself doing some wistful shopping on their website a year or so before that. I remember scrolling down the Dresses page and thinking somebody had designed a collection just for me.

They left Topshop before its closure, launched Tove in 2019, and have since been growing their business slowly and intentionally, following its own needs over industry trends. For instance, they show when it makes sense to do so, and when it doesn’t, they do something else. Today, we are talking about that something else.

articles.title: My First Job in Fashion: Linda Fargo
articles.summary: Fargo, who will receive the CFDA Founder’s Award on Monday, got her start in the display department at Macy’s — a role that eventually landed her a job at Bergdorf Goodman, where she’s worked for three decades.
body: I really didn’t know I wanted to work in fashion. I was an art girl, and my dream was to come to New York. I grew up in Wisconsin, and I couldn’t wait to leave the Midwest. My art form was found objects. I knew I had a real rapport with assemblage and repurposing things. I just didn’t really know how to become a fine artist.

The first job I got was at Macy’s in the display department. For my interview, I bought a vintage 1940s skirt suit at one of the shops on 8th Street and wore it with vintage heels, my hair styled in a French twist. I carried my massive art school portfolio, and I went the wrong way on the subway and ended up on the other side of the river in Brooklyn, with my interview in 20 minutes and no money to take a taxi. Somehow, I made it, and I became the production manager for the window director, and then within four years — by that point it was 1984 — I became Macy’s window director.

articles.title: Food-Themed Fashion Is Starting to Feel Gluttonous
articles.summary: There was a time, not too long ago, when a purse shaped like a baguette felt like a thrilling — even subversive — novelty. Now, we hardly bat an eye when we see that Moschino has made a trompe l’oeil celery purse, or that Big Bud Press is making a hot-dog-and-pretzel-print jumpsuit in collaboration…
body: If you buy something from a link, Vox Media may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Fashion has long found inspiration from the culinary world, but the influx of food-fueled prints, graphics, and trompe l’oeil accessories that picked up steam during the pandemic have now reached a cultural tipping point.

The then-emerging brand made food a central theme of its vision: Its cake-topped aviator caps, Ferrero Rocher heels, and beeswax-sculpted cheese hats — hyperrealistic, absurdist food designs capable of achieving instant social media virality. Prior to working in fashion, Puppets designer Carly Mark was working as an artist whose pieces revolved around candies and snacks. As she told Business of Fashion in 2023, the Puppets universe felt like the ideal pairing given what she considers food and fashion’s motivators: pleasure and money.

articles.title: The Best Top-Handle Bags Will Polish Up Any Look
articles.summary: Shop our edit of the best top-handle bags—this structured style comes in a variety of sizes, from party purses to large totes—from Coach, The Row & more.
body: No handbag trend was more dominant on the fall 2026 runways than the top-handle. Designers across the fashion capitals sent models down the catwalk carrying purses by one or two short straps, putting the handheld style firmly back in the spotlight. But if the phrase “top handle” still conjures images of overly prim bags that look plucked from another era, this season’s assortment will have you reconsidering the once-retro category.

Rather than adhering to one specific aesthetic, the latest crop of top-handle handbags runs the gamut. There are elongated east-west shapes that tap into one of the year’s biggest accessory trends, alongside more relaxed, but equally of-the-moment slouchy options. Practical shoppers have plenty to choose from, too, thanks to roomy totes and bucket bags that work just as well for a morning work commute as they do for a weekend outing. And, of course, there are still the ladylike versions we’ve long associated with the top handle: refined envelope styles and nostalgic kiss-lock purses that can make even jeans and a sweater look elegant.
